note: Also used after negation instead of un/du: je n'ai pas de pain. Becomes d' before a vowel.
ex: Le livre de Marie. — Marie's book.

note: Becomes j' before a vowel or mute h: j'ai.
ex: Je suis fatigué. — I am tired.
Du pain et du vin. — Bread and wine.

note: le/la → l' before a vowel. As object pronoun: je le vois = I see him/it.
ex: Le chat et la maison. — The cat and the house.

note: à + le = au, à + les = aux. Also marks purpose/feature: une tasse à café (coffee cup).
ex: Je vais à Paris. — I'm going to Paris.

note: Also the impersonal 'it': il pleut (it's raining), il faut (one must).
ex: Il fait froid. — It's cold.

note: Also the number one. Plural des = 'some', often left untranslated.
ex: J'ai un frère et une sœur. — I have a brother and a sister.

note: Only for one person you know well, children, family. Otherwise use vous.
ex: Tu viens ce soir ? — Are you coming tonight?

note: Both formal singular 'you' and plural 'you all'. Also object: je vous aime.
ex: Vous êtes prêts ? — Are you (all) ready?

en: in; to; by (+ -ant); of it, some (pron.)
note: Preposition (en France, en été, en train) AND pronoun replacing de + noun: j'en veux = I want some.
ex: J'en ai deux. — I have two (of them).

note: Relative subject 'who/which/that' for people and things: le livre qui est là.
ex: Qui est là ? — Who's there?

note: Always takes a 3rd-person singular verb. In speech it usually means 'we'.
faux: ≠ on — it's a pronoun: we / one / people
ex: On y va ? — Shall we go?
C'est pour toi. — It's for you.

note: dans une heure = in an hour (from now); en une heure = within an hour.
ex: Il est dans la cuisine. — He's in the kitchen.

note: 'It' for feminine nouns: la table → elle.
ex: Elle est médecin. — She is a doctor.

note: Informal form of cela. Ça va ? = How are you? / Is it OK?
ex: Ça coûte combien ? — How much is that?

en: some, any; of the, from the
note: Partitive article (du pain = some bread). Also the contraction de + le = du, de + les = des.
ex: Je bois du café. — I drink (some) coffee.
C'est cher, mais bon. — It's expensive, but good.

en: oneself; himself, herself, themselves; each other
note: Reflexive pronoun of pronominal verbs: se laver = to wash (oneself). Becomes s' before a vowel.
ex: Ils se parlent. — They talk to each other.

note: Object/reflexive pronoun before the verb; becomes m' before a vowel. After the verb use moi.
ex: Il me regarde. — He's looking at me.

en: to the; at the; in the
note: Contraction: à + le = au, à + les = aux. No contraction with la or l': à la gare, à l'école.
ex: Je vais au cinéma. — I'm going to the cinema.

note: Subject, object and stressed form. In speech 'we' is often on.
ex: Nous partons demain. — We're leaving tomorrow.

note: cet before a masculine vowel: cet homme. Add -ci/-là to contrast: ce livre-ci. Also pronoun: c'est, ce que.
ex: Cette maison est belle. — This house is beautiful.

note: un livre sur Paris = a book about Paris; un sur dix = one out of ten.
ex: Le livre est sur la table. — The book is on the table.
Je viens avec toi. — I'm coming with you.

note: Replaces à + place or à + thing: j'y vais = I'm going (there); j'y pense = I think about it.
ex: Il y a un problème. — There is a problem.

note: Also the conjunction 'that' (je sais que…) and 'than' in comparisons (plus grand que). Becomes qu' before a vowel.
ex: Que veux-tu ? — What do you want?

note: Before the verb it means 'to him OR to her': je lui parle. As stressed form = him: avec lui.
ex: Je lui donne le livre. — I give him/her the book.

note: Agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: sa voiture = his OR her car. son before feminine vowel: son amie.
ex: Il aime sa mère. — He loves his mother.

note: mon is used before a feminine noun starting with a vowel: mon amie, mon école.
ex: C'est ma sœur. — This is my sister.

note: Used for a group of all-masculine or mixed nouns/people; elles only for all-feminine.
ex: Ils sont partis. — They left.

note: comme ça = like that; comme il pleut… = since it's raining; Comme c'est beau ! = How beautiful!
ex: Il parle comme son père. — He talks like his father.

note: Stressed form: after prepositions, alone, for emphasis: moi, je… ; donne-moi.
ex: C'est pour moi ? — Is it for me?

note: par jour = per day; par la fenêtre = through the window; par exemple = for example.
ex: Il passe par Lyon. — He goes through Lyon.

note: Object/reflexive form of tu; becomes t' before a vowel. After the verb use toi.
ex: Je te vois. — I see you.

note: Also 'when' after time words: le jour où je suis né. Don't confuse with ou (or).
ex: Où est la gare ? — Where is the station?

note: No accent = 'or'; où with accent = 'where'. ou… ou = either… or.
ex: Thé ou café ? — Tea or coffee?

note: Used with ne: je ne vois rien. De rien = you're welcome.
ex: Je n'ai rien dit. — I said nothing.
Quand il pleut, je reste. — When it rains, I stay.
Un café sans sucre. — A coffee without sugar.

note: Stressed form of tu: avec toi, et toi ?, assieds-toi.
ex: Et toi, ça va ? — And you, how are you?
Deux cafés, s'il vous plaît. — Two coffees, please.
Votre nom, s'il vous plaît ? — Your name, please?

note: ton is used before a feminine noun starting with a vowel: ton amie.
ex: C'est ton livre ? — Is that your book?
Notre maison est petite. — Our house is small.

note: chez moi = at/to my place, home; chez le médecin = at the doctor's.
ex: Viens chez moi. — Come to my place.

note: Mostly plural: quelques amis = a few friends. See also quelqu'un, quelque chose.
ex: J'ai quelques questions. — I have a few questions.
On se voit après le dîner. — See you after dinner.
Le chat est sous le lit. — The cat is under the bed.

note: Formal/written form of ça.
ex: Cela ne me plaît pas. — I don't like that.
Entre nous, c'est nul. — Between us, it's bad.

note: vers midi = around noon. Le vers (noun) = line of verse.
ex: Il marche vers la gare. — He walks toward the station.

note: Replaces de + noun in relative clauses: l'homme dont je parle = the man I'm talking about.
ex: Le livre dont j'ai besoin. — The book I need.

note: avant = before (time); devant = in front of (place). avant de + infinitive: avant de partir.
ex: Appelle-moi avant midi. — Call me before noon.
Oh, c'est joli ! — Oh, that's pretty!
Il mange, puis il part. — He eats, then leaves.

note: Also emphatic in speech: Viens donc ! = Do come!
ex: Je pense, donc je suis. — I think, therefore I am.

en: there is/are; here is; that's it
note: Points to something: voilà le bus. Also 'that's it' and 'ago' (voilà deux ans).
ex: Voilà ton café. — Here's your coffee.
Trois enfants. — Three children.

note: Used with ne: je n'aime ni le thé ni le café.
ex: Ni oui ni non. — Neither yes nor no.

note: Takes the present tense: j'habite ici depuis 2 ans = I have lived here for 2 years.
ex: Je t'attends depuis une heure. — I've been waiting an hour.

note: Only for all-feminine groups; a mixed group takes ils.
ex: Elles sont sœurs. — They are sisters.

note: Merci beaucoup = thank you very much. Le merci = the thanks; à la merci de = at the mercy of.
ex: Merci pour tout. — Thanks for everything.

note: Agrees with the noun. Quel âge as-tu ? Quelle belle journée ! = What a beautiful day!
ex: Quelle heure est-il ? — What time is it?

note: par contre = on the other hand.
ex: Je suis contre cette idée. — I'm against this idea.

note: devant = in front of (place); avant = before (time).
ex: Je t'attends devant la gare. — I'll wait in front of the station.

note: Pronoun with ne = nobody: je ne vois personne. The noun une personne = a person.
faux: ≠ person — as a pronoun means nobody
ex: Personne n'est venu. — Nobody came.

note: Answers pourquoi. parce qu' before a vowel.
ex: Je reste parce qu'il pleut. — I'm staying because it's raining.
Ah bon ? — Really?

note: Stressed form of ils: avec eux, chez eux.
ex: Je vais chez eux. — I'm going to their place.

note: pendant que = while.
ex: J'ai dormi pendant le film. — I slept during the film.
Quelqu'un a appelé. — Someone called.

note: Always singular, followed by a noun. The pronoun is chacun.
ex: Chaque jour, je marche. — Every day, I walk.

note: Possessive: leur maison, leurs enfants. As object pronoun (invariable) = to them: je leur parle.
ex: Je leur donne leurs clés. — I give them their keys.

note: More formal than parce que; cannot start a sentence.
ex: Je pars, car il est tard. — I'm leaving, for it's late.

note: Followed by qui/que/de or -ci/-là: celui-ci = this one; celle de Paul = Paul's.
ex: Je prends celui-là. — I'll take that one.

note: Eh bien = well, so.
ex: Eh bien, on y va ! — Well, let's go!

note: Le derrière (noun) = backside, bottom.
ex: Il est derrière la porte. — He's behind the door.
Quatre saisons. — Four seasons.

note: près de + noun: près de la gare. à peu près = about, roughly.
ex: J'habite près d'ici. — I live near here.

en: from, as early as; as soon as
note: dès que = as soon as; dès demain = starting tomorrow.
ex: Dès demain, je commence. — Starting tomorrow, I begin.
Cinq euros. — Five euros.

note: Points to something near; in speech voilà is used for both.
ex: Voici mon ami Paul. — Here is my friend Paul.

note: Used with ne: je n'ai aucune idée. Almost always singular.
ex: Je n'ai aucune idée. — I have no idea.
Dix minutes. — Ten minutes.
Hé, attends-moi ! — Hey, wait for me!

note: From tenir: tiens / tenez = here you are; Tiens ! = Well, well! / Look!
ex: Tiens, voilà ton livre. — Here, there's your book.

note: Pronoun; the determiner is chaque.
ex: Chacun a son avis. — Everyone has their opinion.
Six heures du matin. — Six in the morning.
J'ai plusieurs amis ici. — I have several friends here.

note: More formal synonym of quand (not used in questions).
ex: Lorsqu'il est arrivé, on a mangé. — When he arrived, we ate.
Dépêche-toi, sinon on part. — Hurry, or else we leave.

note: Emphatic: il l'a fait lui-même = he did it himself. Also elle-même, moi-même, etc.
ex: Il l'a dit lui-même. — He said it himself.
Parmi mes amis. — Among my friends.

note: malgré tout = all the same, nevertheless.
ex: Il sort malgré la pluie. — He goes out despite the rain.

note: Used to get attention, apologize, or ask someone to repeat.
ex: Pardon, où est la gare ? — Excuse me, where's the station?

note: Contracts with à/de: auquel, duquel, auxquels…
ex: Lequel tu préfères ? — Which one do you prefer?

note: Invariable: deux mille. The rare noun un mille = a mile.
ex: Mille euros. — A thousand euros.

note: The adjective sauf means safe: sain et sauf = safe and sound.
ex: Tous sauf lui. — Everyone except him.
Selon lui, c'est faux. — According to him, it's wrong.

note: Cause already known to the listener; not 'since' in time (= depuis).
ex: Puisque tu es là, aide-moi. — Since you're here, help me.

note: Emphatic: je l'ai fait moi-même = I did it myself.
ex: Je l'ai fait moi-même. — I did it myself.

note: Formal; contrasts with cela (that). Rare in speech.
ex: Lisez ceci. — Read this.
Vingt ans. — Twenty years old.

note: un tel homme = such a man; tel que = such as.
ex: Je n'ai jamais vu une telle chose. — I've never seen such a thing.

note: Takes -s in exact multiples: deux cents, but deux cent un.
ex: Cent personnes. — A hundred people.

note: The noun la grâce = grace.
faux: grâce à ≠ grace — means thanks to
ex: Grâce à toi, j'ai réussi. — Thanks to you, I succeeded.

note: Usually hors de: hors de la ville. hors service = out of order.
ex: Hors de ma vue ! — Out of my sight!
Huit jours. — A week (lit. eight days).
Il lit tandis qu'elle dort. — He reads while she sleeps.

note: The p is silent: [sɛt].
ex: Sept jours. — Seven days.
